content.question: How does SMOTE differ from random oversampling?
options: SMOTE generates synthetic minority samples based on a subset of the minority class, instead of simply replicating existing instances.
SMOTE randomly eliminates samples from the majority class until the classes are balanced.
SMOTE adds a penalty to the loss function every time the minority class is misclassified.
SMOTE performs the train-test split automatically before balancing the classes.
content.answer: SMOTE generates synthetic minority samples based on a subset of the minority class, instead of simply replicating existing instances.
